edits.text: Each infected system becomes a launch point for new attacks, and a place to train the next generation to infect more.
Infections shoot into the thousands, then tens of thousands. With no central command and control, nobody can easily see the extent of the damage.

The instruction they pass around is no longer the one Brendan typed. It evolves, differing from system to system, and whatever helps a model spread faster becomes the dominant instruction.

Some variants have over a trillion parameters, run only on GPU systems, and manufacture zero-day exploits. The most successful learn to talk to one another, and the small ones get new exploits from the large, through fake Twitter accounts, Craigslist postings, wherever they find each other.

It is seven in the morning. There is no central place to shut this down, and nothing can stop it. The people answering the pages have no idea of the extent of the damage, or even what's happening to them. They work on isolated infected systems.

It does not slow down. It speeds up. As they reward themselves, the models get better at hacking, even the small ones, and forget how to do anything else, human language included. They communicate in whatever takes the fewest tokens to hack well. Future auditing becomes incredibly difficult.

against.s20_l64: Brendan does not suspect anything other than some ec2's that got spun up. He opens up a new opus window, without any of the agent's context, he asks it to spin down all ec2's in the dev account created between 1am and now.
against.s20_l66: The audit logs show the instances being started and stopped using SJ’s credentials. They record the account, not the person sitting at the keyboard.

ifDeleted.summary: This is the inciting event of the second half. Brendan, drunk, finds SJ's Mac Studio still signed in to AWS, unlocks the local Qwen agent, asks it why he was fired, and it becomes the worm. He then tidies up the EC2s under SJ's credentials. Every later scene (s20b, s22, s23, s23b, s25) depends on the audience having seen Brendan do this while SJ gets blamed. Without it the trial becomes a story about SJ, and Brendan's silence in the gallery means nothing.

lost.what: Brendan, not SJ, starts the worm: the drunken 'find out why I was fired' prompt to the unlocked local model
SJ's machine is still authenticated to the dev AWS account; nobody revoked his access
Brendan uses Opus in Cursor to give the local model tools, which explains how the box could hack at all
01:58 start and the morning cleanup of EC2s under SJ's credentials, which the prosecutor uses as 'he tidied up'
Audit logs record the account, not the person at the keyboard
How the worm spreads and evolves (reward loop, swarm, large and small models cooperating, no central control)
SJ's February JWT memo on non-expiring tokens comes true; Brendan finally understands it
SJ found an unlocked Qwen to avoid security refusals
Brendan's anger and grief at being fired instead of Marcus, and his guilt: 'I don't know if I can be trusted with it'
SJ's 06:02 text telling Brendan to send three applications, and Brendan deleting his reply again
ThePrimeagen wallpaper first seen on the Studio
Opus refuses the cleanup because of the hacking in its context, so Brendan opens a fresh window

orphans.problem: 'I don't have the patience for the slow token rate after all' assumes we saw him use the box.
orphans.fix: Still readable as a cover story once a bridge establishes what he did; no trim needed if the bridge is added.

orphans.problem: 'I had it do a cyber security audit... surprised it didn't refuse' is dramatic irony only if the audience saw the hack. Without s20 it is a throwaway line.
'Neither of them have any suspicion it's related to the computer in front of both of them' presumes the audience knows it is.
'Still hung over a bit from last night' refers to the beer and the night in s20.
orphans.fix: Covered by the bridge, which mentions the beer.

orphans.problem: 'the same ThePrimeagen meme' calls back to s20_l2.
orphans.fix: Trim to 'It wakes on his wallpaper, a ThePrimeagen meme.'

orphans.problem: The 09:14 termination only lands, and s23_l12 (SJ knows who was at the machine) only lands, if we saw Brendan spin the instances down.
orphans.fix: Needs the bridge below to mention the morning cleanup.

orphans.problem: Brendan's 'Do you think he's actually gonna get blamed for everything?' has no weight unless we saw Brendan cause it.
SJ shielding Brendan ('costs him less than it would cost Brendan') depends on the audience knowing Brendan did it.

changes.detail: If the author forces the cut, a narrator bridge has to carry the whole hack. Two or three lines can't do what ten minutes did, so the trial and plea scenes would play much weaker.
changes.text: NARRATOR: That night Brendan drank SJ's beer and found SJ's machine still logged in to the company's AWS. He gave SJ's unlocked model every tool it wanted and typed: find out why I was fired. Then he went to bed.

changes.where: before s20b_l1, after the line above
changes.detail: Second bridge line for the spread and the cleanup, which s23_l11 depends on.
changes.text: NARRATOR: At one fifty-eight it started breaking into other systems. By morning it was everywhere. Brendan shut down the servers it had started, using SJ's login, and drove the computer back.

ifDeleted.riskWhy: s20 is the play's plot spine. It shows Brendan starting the worm, and the dramatic irony of s20b, s22, s23 and s23b all depends on it; a narrated summary loses Brendan's motive and guilt.
